title: CalTrust: Contextual-Bandit Simulation for Adaptive Calibration
oneLiner: A frozen simulation prototype for exploring adaptive selection among calibration interventions.
keyTakeaways: CalTrust implements a LinUCB simulation that selects among four calibration interventions using synthetic user contexts and output features.
An XGBoost proxy is trained on simulated trial data to predict simulated acceptance and confidence outcomes; the training-run metrics were not archived as a report artifact.
The reported policy behavior describes the assumptions of the simulator and synthetic profiles; it is not evidence about human trust or intervention effectiveness.
The contextual-bandit direction is frozen pending real behavioral evidence. InteractionKit is maintained as a separate interaction-specification artifact.
hciRelevance: Provides an inspectable simulation for generating hypotheses about adaptive uncertainty presentation, while making clear that human validation is required before design recommendations are justified.

faq.q: Does CalTrust improve human trust calibration?
faq.a: Unknown. All reported outcomes come from synthetic users and simulated rewards; no participant study has tested the policy.
Additional simulator optimization would not resolve the missing construct and behavioral validation. The reusable interaction-specification work continues separately in InteractionKit.
